meta.title: Carnegie Mellon's Introduction to Programming with Python (High School)

locator_titles.8: Math Functions, Random Values, and Nested Loops

meta.caveat: Five different provenance tiers, kept distinct in the coverage below since they carry very different confidence. (1) California 9-12: CMU's own claim, from the state-specific alignment document CS1's course description links under 'Standard Alignment' ('For state specific computer science education standard alignment visit here'). (2) CSTA 2017, grades 9-10 (3A): mostly CMU's own claim too, from the CSTA alignment table printed directly in CS1's course description PDF (CMU CS Academy, 'CS1: Introduction to Programming -- Course Description and Standard Alignment,' last updated 6/5/23) -- except 3A-AP-18, which that table omits but which CMU's own California document's 9-12.AP.17 claim crosswalks to (a real inconsistency between CMU's two documents, carried here on the strength of the California claim), and 3A-AP-15, which neither CMU document claims and which is this carrier's own addition, mirroring the 9-12.AP.14 argument below: units 3 through 9 are conditionals and loops almost without interruption, and the Creative Task's own design step has students justify which they chose -- the standard's own language. (3) California 6-8, CSTA 2017 Level 2, CSTA 2026 (both Middle School and High School bands), and California CTE (ICT): none of these appear in either CMU document -- CS1 targets '8th or 9th grade with algebra readiness' by CMU's own description, so the 6-8 band is a defensible reach, and CSTA 2026 postdates both CMU documents, which still cite CSTA 2017 throughout. All of these are this carrier's own content-based inference, kept sparse, and every note below says so. Locators throughout are sub-lesson (e.g. '3.2'), from CMU's own 'CS1 Scope and Sequence with Pacing Guide + Example Exercises' (last updated 3/15/23); Unit 9 (Types, Strings, and While Loops) is marked optional in that guide, and its own locator titles say so.

9-12.AP.12.note: Math functions, random values, and nested loops (unit 8) and 2D lists and board-game logic (unit 11) both involve choosing and adapting existing algorithms rather than inventing from scratch.

9-12.AP.13.note: Lists (10.1), list methods (10.2), and 2D lists (11.1) replace repeated simple variables with a single generalized collection -- core, assessed content, not an optional add-on.

9-12.AP.14.note: Woven through every conditionals/loop lesson -- if statements (3.2), if-elif-else (4.1), complex conditionals (5.1), for loops (7.3), nested for loops (8.3), and while loops (9.4, in the optional Unit 9) -- and made explicit in the Creative Task's own design step, which has students list the concepts they plan to use and justify why -- the standard's own language, 'justify the selection.' Not in CMU's own official standards document; the teacher's own classroom analysis argues it should be.

9-12.AP.15.note: Iterative development through events recurs across mouse events (2.2), mouse motion (3.1), key events (4.2 and 5.2), step events and motion (6.3), and the final project (12.1).

9-12.AP.16.note: Helper functions (3.3), introduced right where students first need to break a bigger drawing problem into named pieces, is decomposition into subproblems.

9-12.AP.17.note: Modular design via functions (2.1), methods (4.3), the New Shapes library (7.1), and functions that return values (10.3).

9-12.AP.18.note: Design-for-audience is the Creative Task's rubric, but the rubric itself does not require a feedback step -- CMU claims the standard on the task's design intent; whether it's actually met depends on the teacher building a feedback step in. In this teacher's own classroom it is.

9-12.AP.19.note: Not taught in CS1 -- software license limitations are deliberately deferred to AP CS Principles, where this teacher covers it directly with his own materials.

9-12.AP.20.note: The Creative Task's build-reflect-revise cycle runs ten times a year (units 1-10).

9-12.AP.21.note: Real-time shared-editor pair programming is built into every unit, not a capstone.

9-12.AP.22.note: The Creative Task requires describing the program and reflecting on what changed and why -- documentation of design decisions, ten times a year.

6-8.AP.11.note: This carrier's own inference, since neither CMU document maps CS1 to the 6-8 band: local variables (7.2) is where naming a variable well starts to matter for reading the code back, the standard's own concern.

6-8.AP.12.note: This carrier's own inference: conditionals (3.2), if-elif-else (4.1), compound and nested conditionals (5.1), for loops (7.3), and nested for loops (8.3) are exactly the combined-control-structures, built-up-iteratively territory this standard names.

6-8.AP.13.note: This carrier's own inference: helper functions (3.3) is decomposition into subproblems, the same evidence as 9-12.AP.16 above.

6-8.AP.14.note: This carrier's own inference: functions (2.1), helper functions (3.3), and methods (4.3) are all reusable procedures parameterized for different inputs.

6-8.AP.15.note: This carrier's own inference, same caveat as 9-12.AP.18 above: the Creative Task's design step invites feedback, but the rubric doesn't require it. Whether this standard is actually met depends on the teacher building a feedback step in. In this teacher's own classroom it is.

6-8.AP.18.note: This carrier's own inference: the collaborative task's real-time shared-editor pair programming is team roles and shared tools, the same evidence as 9-12.AP.21 above, at a lighter grain.

6-8.AP.19.note: This carrier's own inference: the Creative Task's describe-and-reflect step is documentation that lets someone else follow what was built and why, the same evidence as 9-12.AP.22 above.

6-8.DA.7.note: This carrier's own inference, and Unit 9 is marked optional in CMU's own pacing guide: types and input (9.1) and strings (9.2) are where the same value can be represented as an int, a float, or a string, and the choice changes what you can do with it.

3A-AP-13.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.12 above, via the castandards-csta2017 crosswalk (strength: partial).

3A-AP-14.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.13 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

3A-AP-15.note: Not claimed in either of CMU's own documents. Same evidence and argument as 9-12.AP.14 above -- this teacher's own classroom analysis, not CMU's claim.

3A-AP-16.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.15 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

3A-AP-17.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.16 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

3A-AP-18.note: Not in CMU's own CSTA alignment table, but CMU's separate California-specific document claims 9-12.AP.17 (modular design), which crosswalks strongly to this code -- a real inconsistency between CMU's two published documents, carried here on the strength of the California claim. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.17 above.

3A-AP-19.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.18 above (crosswalk strength: strong), with the same feedback-step caveat.

3A-AP-20.note: Not taught in CS1, same as 9-12.AP.19 above -- software license limitations are deferred to AP CS Principles.

3A-AP-21.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.20 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

3A-AP-22.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.21 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

3A-AP-23.note: CMU's own claim, from the CSTA alignment table in CS1's course description PDF. Same evidence as 9-12.AP.22 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

2-AP-11.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.AP.11 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

2-AP-12.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.AP.12 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

2-AP-13.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.AP.13 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

2-AP-14.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.AP.14 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

2-AP-15.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.AP.15 above (crosswalk strength: strong), same feedback-step caveat.

2-AP-18.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.AP.18 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

2-AP-19.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.AP.19 above (crosswalk strength: strong).

2-DA-07.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring 6-8.DA.7 above (crosswalk strength: strong); Unit 9 is optional in CMU's own pacing guide.

HS-ALG-PS-02.note: This carrier's own inference -- no CMU source exists, since the 2026 revision postdates CMU's documents: helper functions (3.3) and methods (4.3) are exactly wrapping-repeated-steps-in-a-function territory.

HS-ALG-PS-04.note: This carrier's own inference: random values (8.2) is where a program's behavior stops being deterministic, this standard's own distinction.

HS-PRO-PD-12.note: This carrier's own inference: functions (2.1), methods (4.3), and groups (6.1, CMU's own object-like container for shapes) are all organizing a program into distinct, reusable pieces.

HS-PRO-VD-16.note: This carrier's own inference: lists (10.1) and 2D lists (11.1) are the course's own answer to choosing a structure for a program's data.

HS-PRO-TR-19.note: This carrier's own inference: the Creative Task's reflect step, which asks what was hard and how the design changed, is checking a program against its own original plan.

HS-PRO-TR-20.note: This carrier's own inference: the Creative Task's build-reflect-revise cycle is feedback actually changing the program, ten times a year.

MS-PRO-PD-12.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring HS-PRO-PD-12 above.

MS-PRO-PD-15.note: This carrier's own inference: the collaborative task's real-time shared-editor pair programming is exactly this standard's planning-together, feedback, and shared-tools territory.

MS-PRO-VD-16.note: This carrier's own inference, and Unit 9 is optional in CMU's own pacing guide: types and input (9.1) and strings (9.2) is a program storing and updating more than one kind of data in variables.

MS-PRO-TR-19.note: This carrier's own inference: the Creative Task's reflect-and-write-down-what-changed step, together with the collaborative task's paired work, cover this standard's testing-and-write-up territory.

MS-PRO-TR-20.note: This carrier's own inference, mirroring HS-PRO-TR-20 above.

C4.9.note: This carrier's own inference: functions (2.1), conditionals (3.2), and for loops (7.3) are the branches-loops-procedures-with-parameters-and-variables toolkit this standard names, taught across nearly the whole course.

5.9.note: This carrier's own inference: helper functions (3.3) is the same decomposition evidence as 9-12.AP.16 and 6-8.AP.13 above.
